facts.note: Every numeral on the opening slides comes from this block. An entry with verified:false renders as a claim with no number and greys its slide.

tacit.sentence: Biology design knowledge lives primarily as tacit knowledge: the know-how that makes an experiment work demonstrably does not transfer through publication alone.

literature.cite: Michael Polanyi, The Tacit Dimension, Doubleday 1966 / Routledge 1967, p. 4
literature.what: “We can know more than we can tell.” The origin of the term.

literature.cite: H. M. Collins (1974), “The TEA Set”, Science Studies 4:165–186, doi:10.1177/030631277400400203
literature.what: No laboratory built a working TEA laser from the published sources. Only people with substantial social contact with a successful builder succeeded — phone calls and visits, not papers. Companion: Collins & Harrison (1975), Social Studies of Science.
literature.caveat: Later work (Philosophia Scientiae, 2013) reads the TEA case as RELATIONAL tacit knowledge: knowledge that could in principle be made explicit. That is our claim exactly — the explicit artefact was never built, not that it cannot be.

literature.role: documents it in biology, without ever naming it
literature.cite: Kathleen Jordan & Michael Lynch (1992, 1993, 1998) on the plasmid prep, Social Studies of Science 28(5), doi:10.1177/030631298028005005
literature.what: A protocol every molecular biology lab supposedly shares, and which in practice every lab performs differently — persistent, unresolvable variation in how a shared technique is actually carried out.
literature.caveat: Collins (2001) notes that Jordan & Lynch never use the term “tacit knowledge” and do not engage that literature. Cite them for the PHENOMENON, never as authorities on the term.

tacit.punchline: Biology observed the phenomenon for thirty years and never built the vocabulary for it, let alone the formal object.
tacit.locator: deck/FACTS.md · Polanyi 1966 p. 4 · Collins 1974 doi:10.1177/030631277400400203 · Jordan & Lynch 1998 doi:10.1177/030631298028005005 · Collins 2001 on the Q of Sapphire

mathlib.sentence: mathlib, mathematics’ largest formal library, holds 292,237 theorems over 140,094 definitions, built by 772 contributors.
mathlib.caveat: This is library size, not 292,237 human insights: many definitions and a large share of the theorems are automatically generated (simp, instance and projection lemmas). mathlib is also overwhelmingly human-written, not AI-written.
mathlib.priorFigure: 250,000 theorems a year ago — Rothgang, "Lean and Mathlib", Potsdam colloquium, 17 Dec 2025

formalisationPapers.sentence: In 2026 so far, 688 papers have appeared whose abstracts talk about formalising mathematics in Lean — 148 of them in October alone.
formalisationPapers.query: get_keyword_trends(query="formalized Lean", granularity="year", start_date="2026-01-01", end_date="2026-10-31") over 44,845,581 papers, 9 sources
formalisationPapers.safest: 313 arXiv math.* papers over the same ten months
formalisationPapers.caveat: This counts papers whose ABSTRACT mentions formalising in Lean, not papers that are themselves formalisations. One clear false positive in the top 200 inspected; 200 distinct base ids, so no preprint revision is counted twice. It is one ten-month window, not an all-time total.

biologyFormal.sentence: mathlib holds 292,237 theorems across 34 subject areas — algebra, topology, number theory. Not one of the 34 is biology.
biologyFormal.claimWithoutANumber: Not one of mathlib’s 34 subject areas is biology.
biologyFormal.counterexamples: Formal methods have been used on biology for twenty years: model checking of gene networks, Coq proofs about neuronal circuits, HOL for synthetic biology, and a Lean formalisation of the genetic code posted six days ago (arXiv:2610.36343, Jones & Josephson, 2026-10-26). Every one formalises something biologists already knew, or proves a property of a model.
biologyFormal.narrowFirst: We found no prior formalisation of classical population genetics — Kimura, Fisher, Maynard Smith — in any proof assistant, and no prior system that uses machine-checked biological laws to rule a proposed organism out. That is a negative search result over a 44-million-paper corpus, not a proof of absence.

attrition.sentence: Roughly nine in ten drug programmes that enter clinical trials never reach approval.
attrition.trap: The data are about PROGRAMMES, not individual trials. "90% of clinical trials fail" is a different and false claim, and is the likeliest factual challenge in this deck.
sources: BIO / Informa / QLS 2011–2020: 12,728 phase transitions; Phase 1 → approval 7.9%
Wong, Siah & Lo, Biostatistics 2019 (MIT): 185,994 trials; 13.8% — quote the headline only
Schuhmacher 2025: 14.3% for leading pharma, which cuts the other way
attrition.range: 86–92% across the sources; 14.3% success for the top 20, so "90% of drugs fail" overstates it there
attrition.corrigendum: Wong, Siah & Lo carries a corrigendum (doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxy072) that corrected exactly the phase-transition table. Quote its 13.8% headline, never its per-phase figures.
attrition.locator: BIO/Informa/QLS 2011–2020 · Wong, Siah & Lo, Biostatistics 2019, doi 10.1093/biostatistics/kxx069

negatives.headline: Our headline design fails the physics gate
negatives.detail: The reachable launch speed is 0.67 m/s against a minimum flying speed of 8.64 m/s, and the lifting area is 166× too small: 1.91 cm² against the 317.76 cm² needed to carry 0.007 N.

negatives.headline: An unedited zebrafish scores exactly as well
negatives.detail: The functional-analogue ledger can assess 22 of 73 requirements, and leaves 19 unresolved. An unedited zebrafish scored against the same flying fish leaves the same 19 unresolved: the design’s edits move one row from one hypothesis to another, and neither is a demonstrated resolution.

negatives.headline: Our compensation rule does not predict new cases
negatives.detail: Applied with its case table disabled, the rule chain scores 11 of 12 on the cases it was derived from and 4 of 13 on independent ones. All nine independent errors are false positives: it predicted a compensation response where the experimenters looked and found none. It is kept only in its refusing direction.

negatives.headline: Two of 3,283 interaction edges are zebrafish experiments
negatives.detail: In the molecular pack behind the design, 2 edges are curated zebrafish experiments and 2 more are STRING links whose zebrafish experiments channel reaches 0.4. The other 3,279 are 955 experiments transferred from another species, 1,382 pathway-database assertions and 942 text-mining or co-expression predictions.

negatives.headline: Fifteen of 36 accepted laws can bind nothing
negatives.detail: An accepted law that evaluates nowhere gives false assurance — the law base reads as though a design were checked against it when nothing was. So each of the 15 is listed with a written reason and what would make it bind, and the check fails if an entry stops being true.

negatives.headline: Most of what we published carries no approval field
negatives.detail: 269 of our records are live on the public production nanopub registry. Only the 21 math-biology theorems record who approved the promotion; the 248 Darwin records carry no approval field at all. Their manifest holds a file, an id, a trusty URI, a registry, a timestamp and a commit — and nothing that names a human who signed off.

negatives.headline: Nine of our 12 failed theorems were never attempted
negatives.detail: A failed-theorem record marked attempted:false was never tried at all — the single Lean build lock was contended, or it was abandoned on cost, or withheld on purpose. It is not a result about the statement, and the counts report attempted and never-attempted separately so it cannot be read as one.

deliverables.name: MorphoLemma
deliverables.what: The repository of biological laws — and, just as much, the framework for adding more.
deliverables.how: A new theorem enters the same way every time: upload it nanopub-backed, it must hold in Lean, and it must survive agent debate on the existing evidence. Clear both and it becomes an axiom that constrains every design after it. Fail either and it is recorded with its reason.

deliverables.name: MCP server, API and CLI
deliverables.what: Designed against named personas, use cases and the grand questions — not against a guess at what someone might want.
deliverables.how: 14 personas, 32 use cases, 14 grand questions and 27 ranked tool gaps, served as versioned JSON and checked by tests. The gaps are ranked at build time, and a test tampers with a stored rank to prove no gap can assert its own importance.

deliverables.name: Design Studio (MorphoSwarm)
deliverables.what: Type a phenotype; get the genetic change at every biological layer and every developmental stage.
deliverables.how: Part of delphi-frontier. The laws from deliverable 1 constrain what it may propose, and physics and developmental simulation stress-test what it does.

deliverables.name: The validation harness
deliverables.what: Takes a predicted sequence and a desired function, and says what is wrong with it.
deliverables.how: Finds the closest FUNCTIONAL analogue, annotates every difference interpretably, scores formally in LeanBio, and runs physics on the mesh. Five named results, never summed. It is the thing that told us our own headline design does not fly.

omitted.why: TASK-DESIGN DEFECT: the briefs are infeasible at lawset 1.8.1. All three arms violate the same five binding laws on brief 1, because the sponsor's fixed SL_m 0.25 and mass_kg 0.075 sit outside the Exocoetidae isometry band the accepted laws are scoped to. Re-running lean_check on one arm's own design with SL_m set to the reference specimen's 0.19 drops binding violations from 5 to 0. "accepted" was unreachable by construction, so this stage measures the brief, not the arms. Do not quote its quality column.

merge.rescueNote: A post-hoc re-allocation of the same total budget, unevenly, produced an artifact in every task. It is post-hoc and labelled as such; it was not pre-registered.

limitations: n = 3 tasks per (arm, level). No claim of statistical significance is possible and none is made. A difference smaller than the within-arm min-max spread is reported as NOT separating.

No arm had any tools. Every arm's input was byte-identical. This measures the three architectures as REASONING architectures over fixed inputs; it does NOT measure tool use or tool coordination, which is what the rest of this project actually does. Do not quote it as if it did.

Equal TOTAL budget per cell ($0.45), not equal budget per agent. The single agent gets it in one call; the centralised arm gets a fifth of it per call. Giving every agent the full budget is a different experiment and was not run.
Temperature is not settable through the headless CLI, so runs are not deterministic. Spreads, not point values, carry the information.

panel.finding: The ranking's ORDER held, but its MAGNITUDE did not. On 20 fresh endpoint pairs none of which they used, lazysp_alternate certified 14/20 and q2c_nomodel 14/20, against 13/20 for q2c, collective_shared and collective_isolated - the same ordering as their headline (lazysp = q2c_nomodel > q2c = both collectives), with zero false certificates for every policy. But LazySP's entire margin over q2c is ONE pair, VFVS->ILSG, and it is again a VFVS-start, top-variant-target pair: on the 14 pairs that do not start from VFVS, all five policies resolve exactly the same set, and no pair was resolved by LazySP alone. So the advantage is narrow and structurally concentrated, not broad, exactly as our recount of their own panel found (all 18 of their LazySP-only wins are VFVS-start: 17 VFVS->ALKG plus 1 VFVS->AIKG). The 18-point headline gap is largely a composition effect - 80 of their 100 episodes start from VFVS, versus 6 of my 20 - so on a panel that does not oversample that one family the gap shrinks to 5 points (1 pair). Two further points cut against the headline reading: q2c_nomodel ties LazySP at 14/20, so the GP surrogate is not what buys the win, and LazySP is strictly the least assay-efficient policy on this panel (mean 352.6 assays over its resolved episodes versus 149.2 for q2c), spending more assays than q2c on every single pair both resolved.

rows.label: corrections of our own published claims

items.title: The gja5a fin-length link, withdrawn
items.body: Offered as a second tie to the bioelectric fin-size story. It does not hold: the zebrafish fin-length connexin is gja1b, gja5a has no ZFIN fin record, and Daane’s own text puts cx43 under constrained, not accelerated, evolution.

items.title: The flying-fish genome claim, wrong
items.body: We said almost no molecular data exists for flying fish. An annotated genome does exist, and the error was load-bearing: it was repeated on every number in the map.
items.who: the project lead, not the thread that published it

items.title: A declared null, withdrawn
items.body: We published that no ray-to-interray signalling could be sourced in any fin of any fish. 3 papers contradict it, 1 of them already cited by the same thread on a title-only read. A title-only read was allowed to carry a universal negative; what survives is narrower and none of it pectoral.
items.who: our own curation pass, not the thread that wrote it

items.title: An overstated “settled”, withdrawn
items.body: We said lat4a’s identity was settled on three records. Which gene carries the allele IS resolved to slc43a2a, on the paper’s own chromosome-15 mapping and ZFIN’s allele assignment. Which paralogue carries the flying-fish signal is not: in the paper’s own data both are accelerated, the other more strongly.

corrections.variantMismatch: The zebrafish allele this project's design uses is T200K; the convergent substitution reported in flying fishes is F326L. Different sites, different species, and not the same variant.

envelope.boundsText: η ≤ 0.23, E ≤ 19.35 J/ml, o2Delivery ≤ 0.0187 ml O2/s

corrected.text: Corrected 2026-11-01: the proxies borrowed a snapper cardiac output, and a measured zebrafish at U_crit takes up 2.8× the O2 that ceiling allows (Palstra et al. 2010, PLoS One 5:e14483). With a zebrafish-derived O2 delivery and a skeletal-muscle efficiency the shortfall is about 10 to 30× (central about 20×), not 29 to 38×; 38× is what the original snapper-based proxies give. Sustained aerobic flight is still ruled out by an order of magnitude.

envelope.title: Efficiency and O2 delivery lie in the ranges the cited sources allow (widened after measured zebrafish, v2)
envelope.why: Within the ranges the cited sources support (skeletal-muscle aerobic efficiency up to 0.23, Gladman and Askew 2024; O2 delivery up to the measured adult zebrafish MO2max at Ucrit, Palstra et al. 2010, scaled allometrically to 0.06 kg), the sustained aerobic ceiling at 0.06 kg is at most 0.0833 W. Version 1 claimed "no teleost above 0.0458 W"; measured zebrafish (2630 mg O2 kg^-1 h^-1) exceed v1’s delivery envelope (1350 mg O2 kg^-1 h^-1) about 2x per kg, so that wording was withdrawn. Powered flight at 10 m/s needs 1.346 W, about 16x this ceiling, so the C14 elimination survives.
envelope.scope: Scoped to the sources named, not to every teleost: high-performance pelagic teleosts (tunas) were not fetched and may exceed it. The bound is at one mass (0.06 kg). It bounds SUSTAINED AEROBIC power only: burst power on white-muscle stores is outside it, and that is what a flying fish is understood to use.
envelope.rejectable: Reject it and C14 still rules, but only on the particular proxies a candidate commits.

designval.hashedBefore: hashed before the first number was produced
designval.whoseDesign: YES: Daane et al. 2021 built exactly this double heterozygote and state it phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions. Its measurements are figure-only.
designval.definingAxisWhy: TWO independent reasons, on opposite sides: the baseline has no value and the design has only a figure. This is the axis the whole design claim is about.
designval.phenotypicVerdict: NOT CLOSE, and largely UNSHOWN. 9 of 10 axes cannot be scored. The single scoreable axis scores FAIL at f = 0.00. The axis the entire design claim rests on (pectoral fin length / SL) cannot be scored, and for two independent reasons at once.
designval.consequence: The claim that we can DESIGN an organism is not supported by this validation, and the reason is not that the design scored badly: it is that the design is not measurable on the axes that define it, and the one genetic number that can be computed (1/74) says the design reproduces a single convergent locus out of everything known to differ. Dropping the claim outright under rule 1 overstates what this gate can tell us; the honest position is PREREG rule 2, drop the claim as UNSUPPORTED.
